messages:
jana: RFC follow-up: proposing a write-escrow + spillback pattern for active/active residency violations. sketching behaviour + experiment plan here.

jana: motivation: avoid immediate hard cutovers when a region can't satisfy residency constraints but still accept client traffic. instead, route writes into a short-lived escrow queue and serve reads from the fallback region. preserves availability while preventing premature cross-border writes.

kevin: high level ok. two Qs: 1) what bounds escrow lifespan? 2) how do we ensure eventual delivery without duplication?

jana: lifespan = min(configured_policy, 5m). delivery uses monotonic escrow sequence + exactly-once semantics via compare-and-apply on target primary. escrow entries include idempotency token, tenant_id, original-region, and residency-tag.

priya: detection hooks? how does proxy decide to escrow vs immediate route?

jana: proxies evaluate: X-Residency-Assert mismatch OR control-plane consent=false OR kv-lease-age>threshold. if any of these flipping signals observed for write path, proxy will respond with 202 Accepted + X-Escrow-Id and push payload to escrow service asynchronously. light-weight sync fallback if client sets expect:sync.

ops-jen: operator concerns: how many escrows pending before we trigger operator alert/stop-accepting-writes?

jana: alert thresholds: pending_escrow_count > 2000 per region OR avg_delivery_latency > 30s => page ops. auto-throttle: if pending > 10k, proxies start rejecting new writes with 409 + guidance to retry.

kevin: consistency: if we accept reads from fallback while writes are escrowed, clients might read stale data. are we ok with that for default tenants?

jana: default behaviour is read-your-writes strong only for pinned tenants (sticky session + local cache). for others we document eventual consistency during escrow windows. we can offer a per-tenant opt-in strong path that stalls reads until escrow drain finishes.

compliance-tom: legal gating: escrow still writes PII to any storage location. we need controls to prevent moving PII out of region even queued.
jana: agreed. escrow service will store payloads encrypted at rest in originating region by default. cross-region delivery only occurs if residency policy allows. otherwise escrow is treated as blocked and flagged for manual remediation.

priya: how do we handle failures delivering from escrow to primary if the primary is the problematic region?

jana: delivery flow: escrow -> delivery worker -> target primary via leader-election token. if primary rejects due to residency, delivery worker will consult control plane permission. if still disallowed, escalate and mark escrow as quarantined; operators see quarantined list and can run manual unquarantine after legal approval.

ops-jen: operational tooling: CLI + console views?

jana: tooling: `rw-escrow list --region eu --state pending|quarantined|delivered` ; console panel with live histogram of escrow age, top tenants by escrow size, and one-click pause/unpause delivery per region. deploy-bot will track actions in audit log.

deploy-bot: deploy: escrow-service v1.0 (sha: 7f4c9) rolled to staging-eu and staging-us.

kevin: metrics to create: escrow_count_by_region, escrow_age_p90, escrow_retry_rate, escrow_quarantine_count, percent_reads_stale_during_escrow. alerts: escrow_age_p90 > 2m -> page.

compliance-tom: require logs include tenant_id, escrow_id, residency_flag, delivery_decision but redact payload. retention policy on escrow metadata = 2y for audits.

priya: edge case: a tenant with strict residency gets writes escrowed and operator clears them accidentally -> we must prevent accidental policy circumvent.

jana: implement a two-step unquarantine: operator request + compliance approval for tenants with residency=strict. console will block single-person unlocks for flagged tenants.

kevin: performance: escrow path adds latency for synchronous clients. what's the fallback?
jana: we return 202 by default to indicate async handling. for sync clients we support expect:sync that blocks up to ack_timeout (default 5s) while we attempt local delivery; beyond that we return 202 with escrow id. recommend SDKs use async pattern.

ops-jen: cache warming after delivery: when many escrows drain back to a region, risk of spike. how to smooth?
jana: delivery workers will emit a gradual priming plan to the cache service: batch-deliver metadata and invoke warmup for top-n prefixes, with rate-limits per tenant. backpressure signals can pause delivery.

priya: test plan?

jana: alpha rollout on internal tenants: simulate partitions and control-plane denial for 1-10m, observe metrics and validate quarantined behaviour. chaos tests include delayed kv leases and ack loss. runbooks: how to inspect escrow, how to pause delivery, and how to escalate.

compliance-tom: integration tests to verify encrypted-at-rest in-region and that quarantine blocks cross-region exports. need legal sign-off before beta.

kevin: sample header for clients in staging:
```
curl -X POST https://api.staging.redwood.ai/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Residency-Assert: eu" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: <uuid>" \
  -d '{"input":"do the thing"}'
```

jana: responses: 201 when written locally, 202 + X-Escrow-Id when escrowed, 409 when reject due to overflow or hard policy. all responses include X-Request-Id for tracing.

ops-jen: +1 on alerts & playbook. I'll author the operator runbook and include steps: inspect escrow -> pause delivery -> notify compliance -> escalate.

deploy-bot: experiment scheduled: staging-alpha 08:00 UTC tomorrow, rollback +12h. changelist: escrow-service + delivery-workers + console views.

priya: I'll wire up dashboards and a small synthetic workload to validate read/write behaviour under escrow.

compliance-tom: will review legal gating and provide sign-off checklist by EOD.

jana: thanks team. I'll open the runbook and paste the run id here when it's ready.
